custody.forced_by: Passes the crib's Q2: scope-attenuated, TTL-bounded, fold-enforced at acceptance, revocable, and required for unattended operation.

descriptor.bound: The delegating persona's own membership; the fold rejects any overreach.
descriptor.live: Yes — records must reach honest nodes, which verify them against the fold.
descriptor.reaches: Exactly two execution scopes, storage:state:advance and storage:capability:grant, and nothing else. It signs; it opens nothing. It authorizes only by resolving its delegation chain to a member persona: a chain terminating outside the member roster is void, and generic scope-holding is never consulted for these two scopes.
descriptor.revoke: RevocationRecord plus TTL. Not a ceremony.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing.

custody.forced_by: Persisted in the browser's IndexedDB and usable with no further human interaction until its certificate expires; theft through the page is prevented by WebCrypto non-extractability, and the bound is the certificate validity window plus revocation.

descriptor.bound: The certificate's validity window and scope list.
descriptor.live: Yes — its signatures must reach the dashboard or registry.
descriptor.reaches: The scopes its persona-signed delegation certificate carries (SESSION_SCOPES in network-signon.mjs): delegate:agent, link:publish, link:revoke, tunnel:serve, turn:allocate, and viewer:identify — one certificate per organization persona, all over the single session key.
descriptor.revoke: The certificate validity window (default twenty-four hours, maximum thirty days), enforced at load and by an expiry watchdog that signs the browser out; a root-signed revocation record is the explicit path. Not a ceremony.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing through the page: the key is created extractable:false and _installSession refuses any key claiming otherwise, so no script can export it; it appears in no replicated store.

browser_session_key.notes: Minted per browser during the sign-on ceremony, after the user proves root authority by satisfying the armor's factor policy (password or passkey, per the enrolled policy); routine operations then sign with crypto.subtle.sign and never see a factor again during validity. The crib sheet's section 2 Tier-2 prose conflates this key with a second, different mechanism — the per-operation authorize ceremony, where opening a vault policy class costs one user-verified assertion that derives ephemeral opener seeds (vault_routes.py _openers; factor-management.js _authPasskey) — recorded as crib comments 5ca511cf and its correction for the next synthesis.
signs: registry request envelopes only (REQUEST_DOMAIN + canonical JSON of v, method, path, ts, signer, payload) — the single crypto.subtle.sign call site for this key in network-signon.mjs

custody.forced_by: Released only inside a factor ceremony and never across the release boundary — exporting it would release the whole class.

descriptor.bound: The class's membership at each generation.
descriptor.reaches: Every content key sealed under that class generation.
descriptor.revoke: Factor revocation appends the next generation sealed to the survivors and the anchor; it applies at the next write and touches no existing sealed material.
descriptor.snapshot: The class's secrets for generations this key belongs to.

custody.forced_by: Re-derivable only from the cold factor seed.

descriptor.reaches: The policy shares sealed to it inside the armor envelope.
descriptor.revoke: Factor revocation; the envelope is re-signed without the share.
descriptor.snapshot: Those shares; the policy expression decides what they combine to.

custody.forced_by: Producing it requires the human gesture — typing the password or a passkey PRF assertion (crib Q0).

descriptor.reaches: The factor's derived recipient (its share of the root factor policy) and its derived dashboard access key. Only a factor set satisfying the policy expression reaches the root; unlock-only factors never do.
descriptor.revoke: Factor revocation re-signs the armor envelope without it.
descriptor.snapshot: That factor's policy shares. Whether the root follows depends on the policy expression, not on this key alone.

custody.forced_by: Snapshot is total for its branch, offline.

descriptor.reaches: Every object under the generation and every ancestor via bridges.
descriptor.revoke: None — a generation secret is never retired.
descriptor.snapshot: Total for that branch, offline.

custody.forced_by: Subkeys of the sealed index; neither exists outside a release.

descriptor.reaches: K_index computes blind row addresses; K_meta seals row values. The blind index is the item-to-row mapping; nothing stores it.
descriptor.revoke: Follows the sealed index.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing — they are never at rest.

custody.forced_by: Opened only inside a root ceremony gated on the factor policy.

descriptor.reaches: The root armor it seals.
descriptor.revoke: Re-sealed on every factor change (a new armor generation).
descriptor.snapshot: The armored root, opened only through a satisfying factor set.

custody.forced_by: Derived only from the cold recovery code.

descriptor.bound: The one act; the fold rejects everything else.
descriptor.live: Yes — the rekey event must reach the ledger fold.
descriptor.reaches: Exactly one act: the recovery-authorized door of member.rekey. The genesis_id in the derivation keeps an identical printed code from linking personas across organizations.
descriptor.revoke: Enrolled at member.claim; changing it requires the current member recovery key or the org root. No event adds one after member.claim.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing — no plaintext, no content, no authority beyond the one door.

custody.forced_by: Unique per immutable revision and encrypts nothing else, so releasing it equals releasing that one plaintext — it is the unit allowed across the release boundary.

descriptor.reaches: One object revision's plaintext.
descriptor.revoke: Never — the revision is immutable; withdrawal is a new key for new writes.
descriptor.snapshot: That one revision.

custody.forced_by: Re-derivable from the generation secret during the warm period.

descriptor.reaches: One object revision's wrapped content key.
descriptor.revoke: Follows the generation secret; never individually retired.
descriptor.snapshot: That revision, given the ciphertext.

custody.forced_by: Constitutional acts are intent acts (crib Q0).

descriptor.live: Yes — it must reach the ledger or registry to be used.
descriptor.reaches: Genesis, key rotation, serve-certificate minting, registration, and rebind. It is not a domain principal: it holds no KEM credential and receives no capability grants.
descriptor.revoke: Org-vouch or dual-signed org-root rotation; both are ceremonies.
descriptor.snapshot: No content.

custody.forced_by: An audited vault setting: released unattended once the vault is open; encrypted at rest so a cold dump cannot run the offline location oracle.

descriptor.bound: Location secrecy only; contents keep their own seals.
descriptor.reaches: The row addresses of every secret vault (location, not content).
descriptor.revoke: Re-mint and re-address every secret vault.
descriptor.snapshot: Encrypted at rest, nothing. Held warm, the ability to test password guesses against vault locations offline.

custody.forced_by: The private half derives from the credential's PRF output on-device; using it requires a user-verified assertion at that machine.

descriptor.live: Yes — opening a seal needs the assertion at that machine.
descriptor.reaches: Payloads sealed to the credential's device: cross-device Tier-2 renewals and master-KEK re-wraps. The public key is valid only when carried in a root-signed enrollment statement, verified before any seal is addressed to it.
descriptor.revoke: Passkey revocation (root-signed RevocationRecord).
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing without the device's PRF assertion.

custody.forced_by: Snapshot is zero — it decrypts no existing record; it only receives future distributions while the machine remains in the fleet. Placement is an operator setting.

descriptor.live: Yes — the thief must still be in the fleet and reachable.
descriptor.reaches: Distributions sealed to it after the theft — future persona KEM keys.
descriptor.revoke: Remove the machine from the fleet. Root-signed, not a ceremony.
descriptor.snapshot: Zero. It decrypts no existing record.

custody.forced_by: Snapshot is total: this key plus a copy of the replicated store is the whole domain history, offline. Not disk-eligible at any price.

descriptor.bound: None — damage is complete at the instant of theft.
descriptor.reaches: Every capability grant addressed to this persona, hence any head secret, hence all domain content including full history through the bridges.
descriptor.revoke: Publish a superseding PersonaKemCredential. Stops future grants only; undoes nothing already opened.
descriptor.snapshot: Total for the domain — key plus store copy is the whole history.

custody.forced_by: Deriving it requires the personal root seed.

descriptor.live: Yes — records must reach honest nodes.
descriptor.reaches: Authorship of the persona's ledger events and key-control records in one organization. The genesis_id input keeps personas unlinkable across organizations.
descriptor.revoke: member.rekey moves the persona to a new key.
descriptor.snapshot: Authority to sign as the persona until rekeyed away.

custody.forced_by: Every act needing it expresses human intent (crib Q0), and its snapshot is total; no execution-class question is reached.

descriptor.reaches: Every purpose key ever derivable from it, and every vault policy class through each class's root-anchor wrap. Root authority reconstitutes the whole identity.
descriptor.revoke: None. The remedy is personal-root rotation, which requires the old root, the new root, and the enrolled recovery key (make_rotation in tools/network/idkit/root_rotation.py).
descriptor.snapshot: Total and unbounded, across every organization.

custody.forced_by: Its whole security property is being disjoint from the hot path; it is printed once and never touches a machine except in a recovery ceremony.

descriptor.reaches: Three domain-separated derivations, none reaching another: the armor recovery slot recipient, the recovery signing key, and the per-organization member recovery keys.
descriptor.revoke: Replacement with the code in hand runs replace_recovery_slot (tools/network/idkit/root_factor_policy.py). Regeneration with the code lost is the witnessed succession window: declaration, blocking alert, cancellation or veto, completion after the window.
descriptor.snapshot: The sealed root seed, opened only by the code. No org content.

custody.forced_by: Derived only from the cold recovery code.

descriptor.live: Yes — its signatures must reach a verifier.
descriptor.reaches: The recovery co-signature on personal-root rotation and on recovery-code succession declarations.
descriptor.revoke: Recovery-code succession (the witnessed window).
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing; it signs and never decrypts.

custody.forced_by: Derived only from the cold recovery code.

descriptor.reaches: The root seed sealed into the armor's recovery slot.
descriptor.revoke: replace_recovery_slot re-seals the slot to a new code's recipient.
descriptor.snapshot: The sealed root seed, and nothing else.

custody.forced_by: Sealed to a root-derived recipient; opening it requires root authority.

descriptor.bound: None — it is the root's guaranteed floor under every class.
descriptor.reaches: Every vault policy class, through each class generation's mandatory anchor wrap — the indirection that lets root-factor churn touch only the armor.
descriptor.revoke: Irrevocable by design: revoke_factor refuses to drop it and the store refuses to persist a class generation without it.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing while sealed; every class once the root is open.

custody.forced_by: Exists only in sealed form; released by a factor ceremony.

descriptor.reaches: A sealed store's entire index — its address key and value key derive from it.
descriptor.revoke: Re-mint the store under a new index.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing while sealed; the store's item map once released.

custody.forced_by: Snapshot is none — it reaches no plaintext and authorizes nothing.

descriptor.reaches: Authentication of one outbound serving tunnel (tunnel:serve only).
descriptor.revoke: Re-mint; thirty-day TTL, renewal below twenty days remaining.
descriptor.snapshot: None.

custody.forced_by: Re-derivable only from the cold factor seed.

descriptor.bound: The classes it is enrolled in.
descriptor.reaches: The vault class-key wraps sealed to it.
descriptor.revoke: Vault class-factor revocation reseals the next generation without it.
descriptor.snapshot: Those wraps; each class generation it belongs to opens.

seals: personal_root_seed to the successor code's recovery_slot_recipient

armor.replace_recovery_slot.notes: Built at the armor layer; exposed by no route or UI yet.

writes: next armor generation without the revoked factor

preconditions: Enroll-only; it refuses to overwrite or clear an existing recovery slot.

writes: including the recovery policy declaration when pinned
registry certificate and identity-neutral viewer certificate over the same child

seals: one seal per fleet machine not removed

fleet.distribute_kem.notes: The KEM-distribution record is the unbuilt half of the fleet layer (bead auto-pw9bs.6); the cited theory is its formal spec.

fleet.enroll.notes: Renewal is a new entry with a higher sequence number superseding the old.

writes: root-signed kick tombstone; stops future distribution to that machine

fold.checkpoint.notes: Checkpoint is decided-removed from the design vocabulary; the handler remains in code, so it remains in this inventory.

preconditions: The delegated scope set never exceeds the delegator's (no scope escalation).
A non-redelegable certificate cannot mint children.
Under recovery policy recovery-key, the declared recovery key co-signs the exact transition.
The new key proves control through the continuity signature.
The claim's recovery enrollment is validated here; recovery_pub equal to the org root is refused.

writes: implicit revoke of the departed key on the recovery door

preconditions: The cited old key must be the persona's current key.
A revoked key cannot self-authorize its own rekey.
The new key proves control through the continuity signature.
Under recovery policy none, a recovery-authorized rekey is refused, never ignored.

writes: root-signed enrollment statement binding the per_credential_wrapping_key public half

preconditions: Completion requires the elapsed witness window over a chain containing the declaration and no cancellation and no veto.

writes: fold-inert frontier marker citing all locally current authority heads

rekey.frontier_marker.notes: Without the marker the re-key achieves nothing (the F-001 defect); the calibration theory VaultRekeyF001 demonstrates exactly that.

root.rotation.notes: The auto.network registry pins recovery_pub for personal and org identities (registry/store.py orgs table; the rebind path enforces it in tools/network/registry/app.py). The residual gap is wiring: the armor-layer succession in root_rotation.py does not yet verify against that pin. VaultRootRotationNoDeclaredPk.spthy is the machine-checked acceptance target for closing it.
preconditions: Three signatures — old root, declared recovery key, and new root — verified against the declaration, never against armor contents.

writes: PersonaKemCredential citing the current authority frontier

seals: generation_secret to an unprovisioned member's current PersonaKemCredential
class_key to factor recipients and to root_anchor_seed

preconditions: A member class without the root-anchor wrap is refused at creation and again at the store (put_class, put_root_class_once).

seals: class_key to surviving factors and to root_anchor_seed
writes: next PolicyClassRecord generation; applies at next write

preconditions: The root-anchor wrap cannot be dropped.

autonomy.recovery.signing.v1.description: Derives the recovery signing key from the recovery code.

autonomy/capability-grant/v1.description: Seals a generation secret to a PersonaKemCredential in a CapabilityGrant.

autonomy/personal-owner-at-rest/v1.description: Seals the personal owner key at rest.

autonomy/personal-vault/revision-id/v1.description: Derives a personal vault object's revision identifier.

autonomy/storage-state-secret/v1.description: Domain label for generation-secret material in a StorageStateDescriptor.

autonomy/vault-policy-class/cek/v1.description: Wraps an object content key under a class generation.

autonomy/vault/object-id/v1.description: Derives a vault storage object's identifier.

autonomy/vault/revision-id/v1.description: Derives a vault storage object's revision identifier.
